bull_bear.body: Inorganic: Stöferle acquisition completed Apr-25 (performing above expectations). Organic: Heavy reinvestment in greenfield capacities (AURIC, Chennai, Battery plant). Incentives: Maharashtra PSI scheme enhanced to ₹858cr (GST refund over 7 years).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: 1) Commodity & Energy Volatility: Persistent high gas/oil/alloy prices with lagged pass-throughs. 2) Geopolitical: Middle East conflict impacting shipping/logistics. 3) Regulatory Delay: Potential deferral or modification of ABS mandate. 4) Execution: Ramp-up risks across multiple simultaneous greenfield SOPs. 5) Europe Macro: High energy costs and Chinese OEM competition.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident on volume growth and order book quality; cautious on near-term margins due to external cost shocks (war, commodities); assertive on customer negotiations for price hikes; strategic focus on 'China+1' beneficiaries and EV transition.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: 1) Backward Integration: In-house ECU production for ABS (single-channel started, dual-channel Jun-26) to capture margin leakage. 2) Fuel Switch: Tier-2 suppliers switched from gas to furnace/diesel oil to mitigate availability/cost risks. 3) Aftermarket Tech: First in industry to deploy AI-enabled platform for secondary order maximization. 4) Solar Diversification: Significant non-auto revenue stream emerging (₹345cr wins) from US/Spanish clients.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Stake in the Stoferle entities in Germany raised to 68%, with acquisition of the remaining stake over the next 4 years; the European business invested Euro 6.24 million in Q1FY27 to acquire an additional 8% stake.
- Divested 100% of shareholding in Veicoli Srl, Italy.
- Growth spend is directed at new-order-backed capacity, with FY27 capex of Standalone Rs. 196 Cr and Europe Euro 3.6M and >80% of it in expansion capex and dies.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Braking: ABS capacity expanding by 12L units (SOP Sep-26); Dual-channel ABS SOP Jun-26 (Bajaj); Chennai disc brake plant SOP Jul-26 (Royal Enfield). Suspension: Inverted forks ramping to 100k units/month by FY27 end. EV Electronics: Maxwell turnover ₹162cr (+131% YoY); Battery pack SOP started May-26. Casting: AURIC Shendra SOP Jun-26 (US EV OEM, JLR). Alloy Wheels: 4.8M units capacity; new customers (Honda, Suzuki). Solar: ₹345cr wins (dampers/actuators).
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Raw material inflation and energy costs suppressing near-term margins despite volume growth | Bajaj Auto Ltd | beneficiary | High | Primary beneficiary of dual-channel ABS SOP (Jun-26) and expanded capacity; strong volume growth passed through supply chain. |
| High energy costs in Europe and supply chain disruptions | Tata Motors Ltd | beneficiary | Med | Key winner in 4W casting and braking (SOP Jun-26); benefits from China+1 strategy and local sourcing mandates. |
| Intense competition in EV battery space and regulatory hurdles | Hero MotoCorp Ltd | beneficiary | Low | Potential beneficiary of ABS mandate and suspension upgrades, though transcript notes Hero Electric provision impact on Maxwell (unrelated to core Hero Moto). |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Consolidated Q1FY27 total income splits by entity into India 72.4%, Europe 26.3% and Maxwell 1.3% (Q1FY26: India 69.2%, Europe 29.9%, Maxwell 0.9%).
- Product breadth on consolidated Q1FY27 income: Die Casting 44.5%, Suspension 24.2%, Disc Brake 11.0%, Alloy Wheel 8.5%, After Market 3.7%, Transmission 2.8%, Others 5.3%.
- Consolidated Q1FY27 income by vehicle type: Motorcycle 51.4%, 4 Wheeler 27.0%, Scooter 10.7%, 3 Wheeler 7.3%, Others 3.6%; the standalone book is far more 2W-weighted (Motorcycle 68.4%, Scooter 14.3%, 3 Wheeler 10.0%, 4 Wheeler 5.8%).
- Technology base of 100 total patents and 110 design registrations.
- In Europe the deck flags a structural headwind: "Owing to growing market share of Chinese OEMs, and transition to EV/Hybrid in Europe, we expect reduction in future revenues from currently serviced ICE orders"; ICE end-use is "currently at ~30% of Endurance Europe revenues, is expected to reduce to 25% in FY28."
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Order pipeline] Order book expected to be boosted further with Rs. 4,526 Cr of RFQs under discussion with various customers.
- [Europe demand risk] EU new car registrations in Q1FY27 were 3,074 thousand, up 7.4%, but "Growth in registrations excluding Chinese OEMs was 3%"; registrations remain -14.2% below Q1 FY20 for Total EU.
- [Europe cost base] Italian energy prices rose sharply YoY in Q1FY27: electricity price (PUN) Euro 124/MWH vs 102 (+22%) and Gas PSV 47 Euro cents/cubic meter vs 38 (+23%); versus FY21 these are +183% and +257% respectively.
- [Europe asset write-down driver] Europe profitability was impacted by accelerated depreciation of assets pertaining to OEM programs being phased out.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Standalone margin compressed to 12.5% (vs 13.3% normalized) due to ₹73.7cr alloy/steel inflation (non-value-add) and outsourcing costs (₹31.3cr) from volume surge. Energy costs up 50% (fuel) and 3x (gas vs 2021) in Europe; pass-through negotiations ongoing. Q1FY27 expected volatile; margin recovery targeted from Q2FY27. Maxwell margin impacted by ₹6cr Hero Electric provision.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: Strong double-digit growth expected driven by new SOPs; 4W mix to rise from 6% towards 10%+ medium term. Margin: Q1FY27 volatile due to energy/commodity costs; normalization expected from Q2FY27 assuming pass-throughs. Order Inflow: Robust pipeline (Maxwell RFQs >₹300cr). Capex: FY27 budget similar to FY26 (~₹800cr), focused on automation and new plants.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Total cumulative orders (since FY22, ex-Maxwell/Battery) ₹5,323cr (₹4,593cr new) peaking FY29. FY26 India wins ₹1,596cr (₹1,579cr new). EV-specific wins ₹1,724cr p.a. (incl. Maxwell/Battery). Europe FY26 orders €15.8mn. Key ramp-ups: AURIC Shendra (peak ₹513cr), Battery Pack (₹300-600cr), Maxwell (₹247cr p.a. peak Q2FY27).
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: 1) Regulatory tailwind: ABS mandate expansion to lower cc vehicles (12L new capacity). 2) EV Penetration: In-house BMS/ECU integration increasing value-add; Battery pack SOP for 2W/3W. 3) 4W Diversification: Major wins from US EV OEM, JLR, Tata, Mahindra driving mix shift from 6% to 10%+ revenue. 4) Aftermarket: AI-enabled platform and mechanic loyalty program targeting long-term high-margin growth.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Endurance delivered strong Q4FY26 volume-led growth (Consol Rev +37.3% YoY) driven by 2W recovery and new EV wins, though margins faced pressure from commodity inflation and one-off Hero Electric provisions. The strategic pivot is accelerating with dual-channel ABS, in-house ECU production, and major greenfield SOPs (Battery packs, US EV OEM castings) set to drive FY27-FY29 optionality despite near-term energy cost headwinds.

Target aftermarket contribution of 10% of standalone revenues by FY 2027-28.

Endurance Overseas SpA completed acquisition of a 60% stake in Stöferle Automotive GmbH and Stöferle GmbH, Germany, with a clear pathway towards acquiring the remaining 40% stake over the next five years.

Remain focused on increasing market share in the four-wheeler and aftermarket segments, expanding presence in the premium motorcycle category, strengthening capabilities in advanced technologies and value-added products, and capitalising on emerging opportunities in the EV ecosystem.
Setting up a new aluminium forging facility to support increasing customer demand.
Establishing new capacities across various locations for braking systems, ABS and electronics.
Setting up a lithium-ion battery pack plant at Mindewadi in Pune, Maharashtra, to cater to growing demand from EV and energy storage applications.
Poised to commence production at the AURIC Shendra plant, Dist. Chh. Sambhajinagar, for machined aluminium castings catering to four-wheelers and non-automotive applications.
Remain committed to the Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi), aligning the decarbonisation roadmap with globally recognised standards.

In Europe, maintain discipline in order pursuit prioritising EV and hybrid applications while exploring inorganic opportunities that provide complementary capabilities or access to new markets and customers.

In India, focus on profitable growth through insourcing of high-cost components, securing new business with improved margins and directing capital expenditure towards automation, quality improvement and high-return expansion.
The Chennai plant, at a fairly advanced stage of construction, will have an annual capacity for three million disc brake assemblies and 4 million brake discs.

risks.note: The global economy remains susceptible to renewed trade disruptions and geopolitical escalations; escalating tensions in West Asia could disrupt key energy supply routes and trigger volatility in global oil markets, impacting fuel prices, logistics costs and industrial production.

The industry operates in a dynamic regulatory environment characterised by tightening emission and safety norms and evolving fuel efficiency and Electric Vehicle policies, which drive product re-engineering and compliance investment.
risks.risk: Tightening emission and safety regulation and evolving EV policy

risks.note: Explicitly flagged by the Board as a challenge for the industry alongside the regulatory environment, affecting input availability and cost.

risks.note: The Board flags affordability and financing conditions as demand-side pressures; volume growth in FY 2025-26 was itself partly a function of the September 2025 GST rate rationalisation lowering cost of ownership, making demand sensitive to policy support.
risks.risk: Demand-side pressure from affordability and financing conditions

risks.note: The competitive landscape is intensifying with global OEM participation, new EV entrants and increasing focus on technology, localisation and innovation.
risks.risk: Intensifying competition in the auto component landscape

risks.note: A significant minority share of consolidated total income is generated by overseas operations, and European auto sales grew only modestly (about 1.8% year-on-year in FY 2025-26), so Europe remains a slower-growth, macro-exposed part of the portfolio.
New business wins from OEMs in India are reported excluding orders from one of the Company's major OEM customers, indicating a single customer relationship large enough to be disclosed separately.
risks.risk: Concentration on a major OEM customer

risks.note: Accelerating EV adoption, ADAS advancement and record BEV market shares in advanced markets are reshaping the components industry, requiring continuous reinvestment to keep the ICE-linked portfolio relevant.
